editorial.title: Who Is Deepak Dhar? The Small-Town UP Boy Who Studied Under Feynman — and Just Joined Physics' Most Exclusive Club
editorial.excerpt: The 74-year-old Indian theoretical physicist just won the 2026 Dirac Medal, becoming the first Indian-born recipient. His journey from Pratapgarh to Caltech to the pinnacle of world physics — and the sandpile that connects it all to AI.
editorial.image_caption: Deepak Dhar, INSA Distinguished Professor at ICTS-TIFR Bengaluru. The 74-year-old theoretical physicist won the 2026 ICTP Dirac Medal for his contributions to statistical mechanics.

sources.label: IIT Kanpur - Prof Deepak Dhar Interview

editorial.nri_angle: Deepak Dhar's journey from a small-town UP childhood to Caltech and back to India, winning honors that place him among Hawking and Witten, represents the deep scientific contributions of Indian-origin minds that often go uncelebrated compared to tech industry success stories.
editorial.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.excerpt: The veteran character actor and dialogue writer takes on the most dramatic role of his career in Netflix India's most expensive production.
just_in.image_caption: A still from Netflix's Operation Safed Sagar, the streamer's most expensive Indian production based on the IAF's role in the 1999 Kargil War. The series features Manu Rishi Chadha as General Pervez Musharraf.

just_in.title: Indian Chemist Gautam Desiraju Wins Crystallography's Highest Honor, the Ewald Prize
just_in.excerpt: The IISc professor emeritus and grandson of India's second President is recognized for pioneering crystal engineering over a five-decade career.
just_in.image_caption: Gautam R. Desiraju, professor emeritus at the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. He has been awarded the 14th Ewald Prize for his foundational work in crystal engineering.
just_in.nri_angle: Desiraju earned his PhD at the University of Illinois and conducted research at Eastman Kodak before returning to India, embodying the diaspora-to-homeland knowledge pipeline.

just_in.nri_angle: The leadership upheaval at India's largest conglomerate directly affects global investors with exposure to TCS and Tata Motors, two of the most widely held Indian ADRs.

just_in.title: Air India Pilot Confirmed Positive for Marijuana as Crew Reveals Erratic Cockpit Behavior
just_in.excerpt: The captain of the Phuket-Delhi flight that dropped 300 feet could not walk properly after landing and tried to smoke in the cockpit, cabin crew told the airline in a formal complaint.
just_in.image_caption: An Air India Airbus A320 aircraft on the tarmac. The pilot-in-command of the Phuket-Delhi flight has failed his confirmatory drug test for marijuana, with cabin crew filing a formal complaint about his erratic behavior.
just_in.nri_angle: The incident deepens safety concerns for the millions of Indian diaspora members who rely on Air India for long-haul flights between India and destinations worldwide.

just_in.excerpt: The revocations — up 75% from the 100,000 milestone announced in January — target criminal activity, birth tourism, and political speech, as Indian student visa approvals drop 60%.

just_in.nri_angle: Indian student visa approvals have dropped 60% under Trump's visa crackdown, and the broader revocation campaign affects Indians holding work, student, and immigrant visas.

news.title: Jainendra Jain Becomes First Indian-Origin Physicist to Win Wolf Prize
news.excerpt: The Penn State professor and Rajasthan native received the 2025 Wolf Prize in Physics for his discovery of composite fermions, a breakthrough central to quantum computing research.
news.image_caption: Prof. Jainendra K. Jain at the Wolf Prize ceremony in Jerusalem. The Penn State physicist is the first person of Indian origin to receive the Wolf Prize in Physics.
news.nri_angle: Jainendra Jain becomes the first Indian-origin scientist to win the Wolf Prize in Physics, drawing a direct line from rural Rajasthan to the pinnacle of global physics recognition.

news.title: Andhra Pradesh Student Dileep Kumar Bungatavula Killed in Ohio After Pick-Up Truck Rams His Car Head-On
news.excerpt: The North America Telugu Society has launched a fundraiser to support the student's farming family back in Andhra Pradesh, adding to a grim toll of Indian student road fatalities in the US.
news.image_caption: The Prentice Memorial Gateway at Kent State University in Kent, Ohio. Dileep Kumar Bungatavula, a student from Andhra Pradesh based in Kent, was killed in a head-on collision with a pick-up truck.
news.nri_angle: Indian student from Andhra Pradesh killed in Ohio; Telugu diaspora organizations mobilize fundraising for his farming family.

news.title: US Judge Dismisses Criminal Charges Against Gautam Adani After DOJ Abandons Bribery Case
news.excerpt: Brooklyn federal judge grants rare DOJ request to drop 2024 fraud and bribery indictment, ending a high-profile prosecution that spanned two presidential administrations.
news.image_caption: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group. A US federal judge dismissed criminal bribery charges against Adani on Monday after the Department of Justice moved to abandon the case.
news.nri_angle: The dismissal of charges against India's second-richest person removes a cloud over Adani Group's US investment plans and signals a shift in how American courts handle cross-border corporate cases.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.excerpt: A violent flash flood in Chamoli district swept away a bridge and a vehicle on the Jyotirmath-Malari highway, cutting off over a dozen border villages as monsoon fury continues across the state.
news.image_caption: A footbridge destroyed by floodwaters over the Mandakini river in Uttarakhand. Flash floods in Chamoli district ripped apart a bridge on the Jyotirmath-Malari highway, cutting off villages in the Niti Valley.
news.nri_angle: The Niti Valley bridge collapse disrupts a key route to Hindu pilgrimage sites near Badrinath, affecting NRI travelers planning Char Dham yatra during the monsoon season.

nri-world.excerpt: The India Heritage Preservation Council celebrated the American author and Vedic scholar who spent over 40 years studying and promoting Indian spiritual heritage.

nri-world.excerpt: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan's four-day trip and an Indian Army contingent's march in Côte d'Ivoire's Independence Day parade mark New Delhi's growing military footprint across Africa.
nri-world.image_caption: Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan during his visit to Mauritius for maritime security talks. The visit is part of India's expanding defence outreach across the Indian Ocean and Africa.
nri-world.nri_angle: Mauritius has the largest proportional Indian-origin population of any country, with roughly two-thirds of its residents tracing ancestry to the subcontinent. India's defence outreach to Africa also extends a security umbrella to Indian diaspora communities across the continent.

nri-world.title: Indian Universities Nearly Quintuple Presence in QS World Rankings Since 2015 as IIT Delhi Hits Record 118th
nri-world.excerpt: India now has 52 universities in the QS World Rankings, up from 11 a decade ago, with IIT Delhi achieving the highest position ever for an Indian institution.
nri-world.image_caption: IIT Delhi campus, India's highest-ranked university in the QS World Rankings 2027 at 118th globally. India now has 52 universities in the rankings, up from 11 in 2015.
nri-world.nri_angle: India's fivefold increase in globally ranked universities expands options for diaspora families considering Indian institutions and signals growing international recognition of Indian higher education.

nri-world.title: From Barren Land to Cricket's Premier Hub: How Jay Shah Built the BCCI Centre of Excellence
nri-world.excerpt: The 40-acre Bengaluru facility has drawn Hardik Pandya as its first permanent resident and Bangladesh's cricket board for a study visit, but a fitness communication breakdown has put its sports science operations under review.
nri-world.image_caption: The BCCI Centre of Excellence was inaugurated by Jay Shah and Roger Binny in Bengaluru in September 2024. The 40-acre facility has become central to Indian cricket training and rehabilitation operations.
nri-world.nri_angle: The BCCI Centre of Excellence represents India's biggest investment in cricket infrastructure, directly affecting how India's stars prepare for ICC events that diaspora fans follow closely, and drawing international study visits from Bangladesh.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Canadian Police Arrest Suspect Seven Months After Indian-Origin Woman Himanshi Khurana Murdered in Toronto
nri-world.excerpt: Abdul Ghafoori, 32, faces first-degree murder charges after a Canada-wide manhunt following the December 2025 killing classified as intimate partner violence.
nri-world.image_caption: Toronto Police had issued a Canada-wide warrant for Abdul Ghafoori after Himanshi Khurana was found dead in December 2025. Ghafoori has now been arrested approximately seven months later.
nri-world.nri_angle: The murder and subsequent manhunt highlighted safety concerns for Indian nationals in Canada and prompted diplomatic intervention from the Indian Consulate General in Toronto.
